title: Samsung Electronics locks in 80% of next year’s memory output through long-term deals
source_used: KED Global (text read on Bloomingbit's English feed)
key_facts: Samsung Electronics has secured nearly 80% of next year's memory output, including high-bandwidth memory, under long-term supply agreements, according to industry officials on 9 Oct 2026.
Nvidia, Google and Microsoft are among the technology companies that have placed orders with Samsung covering more than five years of chip supply.
Companies without contracts are competing behind the scenes for the remaining roughly 20% of output.
SK Hynix and Micron have also signed large long-term agreements; Micron's strategic customer agreements rose to 26 in Q3 from 16 in Q2.

The trend is spreading to MLCCs (small capacitors), FC-BGA substrates, transformers and power equipment, and cooling systems; Samsung Electro-Mechanics is preparing a 700 billion won MLCC deal with Delta Electronics.
Samsung said on its second-quarter call that 'nearly all major customers are requesting LTAs' and that it is 'difficult to respond to all of those requests'.
quote_evidence: Samsung Electronics has secured nearly 80% of next year's output of memory semiconductors, including high-bandwidth memory, under long-term supply agreements, according to industry officials.
Big Tech companies that have yet to sign contracts with Samsung will have to compete behind the scenes for the remaining roughly 20% of output.
The shift is no longer limited to memory.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory is so scarce that buyers are locking in supply for years ahead.
